prose: Short note from feed metadata only: the Wall Street Journal (Gunjan Banerji) reports that the cost of insuring against debt defaults at the AI hyperscalers - Amazon, Alphabet, Microsoft, Meta and Oracle - has hit its highest level since 2021, as investors, traders and tech executives hunt for protection on trillions of dollars riding on the AI trade. The source is paywalled, so the specific credit-default-swap levels and the mechanics of who is buying are unverified here.
highlights: WSJ: default insurance on hyperscaler debt (Amazon, Alphabet, Microsoft, Meta, Oracle) at its highest cost since 2021
Trillions riding on the AI trade have investors and executives hunting for protection
Credit-default-swap market as the tell for AI-bubble anxiety
